aeon-html-template.comment: Only matches a template literal immediately preceded by the `html` tag identifier — this is what keeps a plain (untagged) template literal from ever picking up Aeon/HTML highlighting.
aeon-html-template.name: meta.embedded.block.html.aeon

aeon-interpolation.comment: A `${...}` interpolation inside the html`` body. Matched before the generic HTML include so its JS contents don't get misparsed as markup, and so it doesn't swallow the closing backtick of the outer template on a stray `}`.
aeon-interpolation.name: meta.embedded.line.js.aeon

aeon-tag.comment: A single HTML start tag, scanned attribute-by-attribute so each of Aeon's four binding-prefix kinds (.prop= @event= ?bool= attr=) gets its own distinct scope before falling back to the built-in HTML tag grammar for everything else (tag name, plain attributes, quotes).
aeon-tag.name: meta.tag.aeon

aeon-property-binding.comment: Aeon's `.prop=` DOM-property binding — el[name] = value (see dom.js's `kind === 'property'` branch). Distinct scope from a plain attribute so it reads visually different.

aeon-event-binding.comment: Aeon's `@event=` listener binding — el.addEventListener(name, value) (see dom.js's `kind === 'event'` branch).

aeon-boolean-binding.comment: Aeon's `?bool=` boolean-attribute binding — el.toggleAttribute(name, !!value) (see dom.js's `kind === 'boolean'` branch).

aeon-plain-attribute.comment: A plain `attr=` binding (or a static, non-bound attribute) — el.setAttribute(name, value). Kept as the normal HTML attribute-name scope on purpose (no `.aeon` suffix) since this is the one kind that should look exactly like ordinary HTML.
